package_info.package_versions: N/A (potentially all versions at time of compromise)
package_info.why_malicious: The official PHP source code repository was compromised, and attackers attempted to insert a backdoor into the PHP core. This would have enabled remote code execution on any server running a compromised PHP binary, impacting all downstream users and websites relying on PHP. The malicious commit was designed to introduce unauthorized code into the core PHP distribution, violating supply chain trust and potentially enabling widespread exploitation.

execution_context.trigger: At HTTP request handling (runtime, when PHP processes a request)
execution_context.file_location: php-src/main/main.c (exact file: ext/zlib/zlib.c, as per public incident details)
required_permissions: filesystem (to read and execute PHP code)
network (if the executed code initiates outbound connections)
process execution (if arbitrary code is run)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At HTTP request handling, the code checks if the HTTP User-Agent header contains the string 'zerodium', then uses zend_eval_string to execute arbitrary PHP code provided in the request, allowing remote code execution on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code introduces a hidden backdoor that allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary PHP code on any server running the compromised PHP binary, triggered by a specific User-Agent value. The use of zend_eval_string in core PHP, gated by an obscure trigger, is highly anomalous and dangerous.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate PHP source code should never contain hidden triggers or code execution paths based on HTTP headers, especially not in production builds. Core PHP should not allow arbitrary code execution based on untrusted input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Conditional code based on HTTP headers may be used in debugging or test environments, but never in production or public releases, and never to enable arbitrary code execution via hidden triggers.
key_indicators: Conditional execution based on a specific, obscure HTTP header value ('zerodium' in User-Agent)
Use of zend_eval_string to execute arbitrary PHP code in core source files
Presence of hidden triggers in production code
Unexpected code paths in core PHP files that enable remote code execution

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains unauthorized access to the official PHP Git server and injects a malicious commit containing a backdoor.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is merged into the PHP source code repository.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is distributed to users and organizations who download or build PHP from the compromised repository.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromised PHP binaries are deployed on production servers.

attack_chain.action: At runtime, if an HTTP request with a User-Agent containing 'zerodium' is received, the backdoor executes arbitrary PHP code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote code execution on affected servers.

behavioral_signatures: Conditional code execution in core PHP files based on specific HTTP header values (e.g., User-Agent containing 'zerodium')
Use of zend_eval_string or similar code execution functions in unexpected locations within the PHP source code
Presence of hidden triggers that enable arbitrary code execution in production builds
file_indicators: Unexpected changes or commits in core PHP source files such as main.c or zlib.c
Presence of code referencing 'zerodium' or similar hardcoded trigger strings in the PHP source code
Unexplained use of zend_eval_string in core PHP files
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with User-Agent: zerodium or similar suspicious values
Outbound connections initiated by PHP processes in response to crafted requests (if attacker-supplied code initiates callbacks)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor for unauthorized or suspicious commits in core PHP repositories. Scan source code for conditional execution paths based on HTTP headers and for use of zend_eval_string or similar functions in core files. Deploy runtime monitoring to detect unexpected code execution triggered by specific HTTP headers, and alert on HTTP requests with suspicious User-Agent values such as 'zerodium'. Audit production PHP binaries for unauthorized code paths and hidden triggers.
